candidates.label: NewsMediaOrganization
candidates.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

types.oie_definition: A quantitative relationship indicating a part of a whole, often expressed as a fraction or percentage.
types.embedding_query_text: Proportion: A quantitative relationship indicating a part of a whole, often expressed as a fraction or percentage. Also called ratio, fraction, percentage.

chosen_type.label: QuantitativeValue
chosen_type.justification: The mention '1%' is a numerical value indicating proportion, fitting the QuantitativeValue schema.

mentions: 1% of the material in archives and libraries around the world

candidates.label: QuantitativeValueDistribution
candidates.comment: A QuantitativeValueDistribution is a StructuredValue representing a statistical distribution of values. Also called value distribution, statistical range. Examples: the average height of a population with standard deviation, a product's price distribution across different retailers, a range of test scores with median and mode.

candidates.label: QuantitativeValue
candidates.comment: A QuantitativeValue is a StructuredValue representing a point value or interval for product characteristics or other purposes. Also called numerical value, measurable value. Examples: a product's weight of '5 kg', a temperature range of '20-25°C', a height of '1.8 meters', a price of '$99.99'. Distinct from QualitativeValue, which represents a predefined, non-numeric value.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmountDistribution
candidates.comment: A quantitative value distribution representing a statistical distribution of monetary amounts. Also called money distribution, financial range, income distribution. Examples: "average salary range", "distribution of asset values", "price range for a product category".

candidates.label: Integer
candidates.comment: Integer is a data type representing a whole number without a fractional component. Also called whole number, natural number (if positive), counting number. Examples: 0, 1, -5, 1000. Distinct from Float, which includes decimal values.

types.oie_definition: A portion or excerpt of a larger text, often analyzed independently for specific information.
types.embedding_query_text: Text Segment: A portion or excerpt of a larger text, often analyzed independently for specific information. Also called text excerpt, document fragment, written segment.

chosen_type.label: Clip
chosen_type.justification: The 500-symbol extract is a short segment of a larger text, fitting the Clip schema.

candidates.label: Clip
candidates.comment: A short segment or part of a larger audio or video program. Also called segment, excerpt, snippet, short video. Examples: A news clip, a movie trailer, a highlight reel from a sports game, a sound bite. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is the broader category for any creative content.

candidates.label: Chapter
candidates.comment: A distinct section or division within a larger creative work, typically a book. Also called book section, segment, part, installment. Examples: Chapter 1 of "Moby Dick", the introduction chapter, the final chapter.

candidates.label: TextDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A digital document primarily composed of textual content. Also called text file, digital document, e-document. Examples: a PDF report, a Word document, an e-book. Distinct from TextObject, which is a media object representing a text file, often for embedding or linking.

candidates.label: Text
candidates.comment: A fundamental data type representing a sequence of characters. Also called string, character data, plain text. Examples: "Hello World", "123 Main St", "product description".

candidates.label: TVClip
candidates.comment: A short segment or part of a television program. Also called TV segment, television excerpt, show clip, broadcast snippet. Examples: a highlight reel from a TV show, a news report segment, a commercial break.
